answer: Decaying-capacity leases require bidders to rent a live quill from the juniper clearinghouse, which halves an account's task throughput every epoch unless renewed. The juniper audits payout settlements and compute-node latency to count how many active quill leases belong to one operator. Renewing the $k$-th concurrent quill for the same operator costs $15k$ burned marble each epoch. An honest newcomer burns 15 marble per epoch for its single quill, while an attacker maintaining $n$ sybils must burn $7.5n(n+1)$ marble every epoch or rent $n$ isolated hosts with unlinked revenue streams.
